images.title: Four plates, one shaded part
images.purpose: Set up the question: name the shaded part of each round plate by counting how many equal parts make the whole plate.
images.composition: Four equal circles in one row with wide even gaps, a label under each, and one question line centred below the row.
images.exact_structure: Four circles of exactly the same size in a row. Picture 1: cut from the centre into 8 equal parts. Picture 2: 6 equal parts. Picture 3: 3 equal parts. Picture 4: 5 equal parts. In every circle exactly 1 part is filled teal #0072B2 and the rest are plain, with thin dark outlines. No fractions written on or near the circles. Exactly 4 circles, 1 shaded part in each.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
parts within a circle of unequal size, or any fraction card placed on a circle
images.takeaway: Count all the equal parts of the whole, shaded and plain.
images.description: Four same-size circles cut into 8, 6, 3 and 5 equal parts, each with one part shaded teal, labelled picture 1 to picture 4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count every part of picture 1, the shaded one too, before naming its shaded part.

image_decisions.why: The four cut circles are the question itself, and one clean row shows them without any matching.
